The CF gauge follows from the exact transmutation of a boson into a fermion bound to one flux quantum, ℒB​[X]=ℒF​[X+γ]−14​π​γ​d​γ\mathcal{L}_{B}[X]=\mathcal{L}_{F}[X+\gamma]-\frac{1}{4\pi}\gamma\,d\gamma: the CFs couple to u=a+γu=a+\gamma and see αs=α−1\alpha_{s}=\alpha-1. For semions (m=2m=2) the unimodular change of variables to uu and w=2​a+γw=2a+\gamma gives 24​π​a​d​a−14​π​γ​d​γ=−24​π​u​d​u+14​π​w​d​w\frac{2}{4\pi}a\,da-\frac{1}{4\pi}\gamma\,d\gamma=-\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du+\frac{1}{4\pi}w\,dw, so ww decouples from the matter, and integrating it out leaves the CF form of Eq. (S40) with the parent FCI (uu is the CF-gauge aa of the main text),

ℒ=ℒF​[u]−24​π​u​d​u−12​π​Ac​d​u−14​π​Ac​d​Ac.\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{F}[u]-\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du-\frac{1}{4\pi}A_{c}\,dA_{c}. (S42)

At θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3 the CF level 1/αs=−3/21/\alpha_{s}=-3/2 is not an integer, and we keep aa and γ\gamma separate (Sec. S3.3).

S3.2 Semions: superfluid of pairs

At ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 the CFs fill two levels of the positive field b¯\bar{b}. Integrating them out gives their Hall response and a Maxwell term set by the CF cyclotron gap. With Eq. (S42),

ℒ=24​π​u​d​u−24​π​u​d​u−12​π​Ac​d​u−14​π​Ac​d​Ac+ϵ2​𝐞2−12​μ​b2=−12​π​Ac​d​u−14​π​Ac​d​Ac+ϵ2​𝐞2−12​μ​b2.\begin{split}\mathcal{L}&=\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du-\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du-\frac{1}{4\pi}A_{c}\,dA_{c}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}\mathbf{e}^{2}-\frac{1}{2\mu}b^{2}\\ &=-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du-\frac{1}{4\pi}A_{c}\,dA_{c}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}\mathbf{e}^{2}-\frac{1}{2\mu}b^{2}.\end{split} (S43)

The Chern–Simons term of uu cancels exactly. A pure Maxwell field in 2+1 dimensions is dual to a compact scalar σ\sigma, 12​π​ϵμ​ν​λ​∂νuλ∝∂μσ\frac{1}{2\pi}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\lambda}\partial_{\nu}u_{\lambda}\propto\partial^{\mu}\sigma, and the coupling −12​π​Ac​d​u-\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,du means that σ\sigma is the phase of a superfluid [9, 8]. The condensed boson is a pair of semions. For SU(2) semions there is also a quantized spin Hall response: with a probe AsA_{s} that couples to SzS_{z} with charge ±1\pm 1, the response 14​π​∑±(u±As)​d​(u±As)=24​π​u​d​u+24​π​As​d​As\frac{1}{4\pi}\sum_{\pm}(u\pm A_{s})d(u\pm A_{s})=\frac{2}{4\pi}u\,du+\frac{2}{4\pi}A_{s}\,dA_{s} gives Eq. (S43) for the charge and the spin Hall term 24​π​As​d​As\frac{2}{4\pi}A_{s}\,dA_{s} of the gapped spin sector.

The pairs in the wavefunction.

On the plane, with ℓ∗=(πn)−1/2\ell^{*}=(\pi n)^{-1/2} and G=∏ie−|zi|2/4ℓ∗2G=\prod_{i}\mathrm{e}^{-|z_{i}|^{2}/4\ell^{*2}}, the semion states are ΦF=χ2​G=det[zik|z¯i​zik]​G\Phi_{F}=\chi_{2}G=\det[z_{i}^{k}\,|\,\bar{z}_{i}z_{i}^{k}]G (spinless) and ΦF=Δ⁡(z)​Δ​(w)​G\Phi_{F}=\Delta(z)\Delta(w)G [SU(2), zz (ww) the up (down) coordinates]. Putting the up and down members of a pair at the same point RR gives exactly

ΦF(R,R,Z′)=±e−|R|2/2ℓ∗2∏k∈Z′(zk−R)ΦF(N−2)(Z′).\Phi_{F}(R,R,Z^{\prime})=\pm\mathrm{e}^{-|R|^{2}/2\ell^{*2}}\prod_{k\in Z^{\prime}}(z_{k}-R)\,\Phi_{F}^{(N-2)}(Z^{\prime}). (S44)

For the spinless state, with the members at RR and R+εR+\varepsilon, χ2​(R,R+ε,Z′)=ε¯​A+ε​B+O⁡(ε2)\chi_{2}(R,R+\varepsilon,Z^{\prime})=\bar{\varepsilon}A+\varepsilon B+O(\varepsilon^{2}), and a row operation and a Laplace expansion give A=±e−|R|2/2ℓ∗2∏k(zk−R)χ2(N−2)(Z′)A=\pm\mathrm{e}^{-|R|^{2}/2\ell^{*2}}\prod_{k}(z_{k}-R)\,\chi_{2}^{(N-2)}(Z^{\prime}) exactly; the ε¯\bar{\varepsilon} channel condenses. The two members contribute the statistical factor ∏k[(zk−R)/|zk−R|]2​αs=∏k(zk−R)−1​|zk−R|\prod_{k}[(z_{k}-R)/|z_{k}-R|]^{2\alpha_{s}}=\prod_{k}(z_{k}-R)^{-1}|z_{k}-R|, which cancels the vortex:

Ψ(pair at R;Z′)=ϕpair(ε)WR(Z′)Ψ(N−2)(Z′),WR=e−|R|2/2ℓ∗2∏k|zk−R|>0.\Psi(\text{pair at }R;Z^{\prime})=\phi_{\rm pair}(\varepsilon)\,W_{R}(Z^{\prime})\,\Psi^{(N-2)}(Z^{\prime}),\qquad W_{R}=\mathrm{e}^{-|R|^{2}/2\ell^{*2}}\prod_{k}|z_{k}-R|>0. (S45)

The amplitude for the pair at RR is positive and nodeless, as in Feynman’s argument for bosons, and since ⟨∑kln⁡|zk−R|⟩=π​n2​|R|2+\langle\sum_{k}\ln|z_{k}-R|\rangle=\frac{\pi n}{2}|R|^{2}+const the pair sees no net field. Cauchy’s identity det[1/(zi−wj)]=±Δ(z)Δ(w)/∏i​j(zi−wj)\det[1/(z_{i}-w_{j})]=\pm\Delta(z)\Delta(w)/\prod_{ij}(z_{i}-w_{j}) writes the SU(2) state as a number-projected BCS state of up–down semion pairs with the CF pair function 1/(z−w)1/(z-w), times a Jastrow factor [89].

Pair coherence.

The pair density matrix ρ2​(R,R′)∝⟨WR​WR′⟩N−2\rho_{2}(R,R^{\prime})\propto\langle W_{R}W_{R^{\prime}}\rangle_{N-2} has no sign problem. In the bare state the CF density is incompressible, S⁡(q)=q2​ℓ∗2/2S(q)=q^{2}\ell^{*2}/2, so ln⁡WR=∫ρ​ln⁡|𝐫−R|\ln W_{R}=\int\rho\ln|\mathbf{r}-R| is log-correlated and C2=ρ2​(R,R′)/ρ2​(R,R)∝(ℓ∗/d)ν∗/2C_{2}=\rho_{2}(R,R^{\prime})/\rho_{2}(R,R)\propto(\ell^{*}/d)^{\nu^{*}/2}: only algebraic pair order. True off-diagonal order needs S⁡(q)∝qS(q)\propto q, in a Jastrow language a factor ∏i<j|wi​j|−1/2\prod_{i<j}|w_{ij}|^{-1/2} that removes the log kernel together with a Reatto–Chester tail [90]. In our wavefunctions the backflow and the Jastrow factor cure this: the pair correlations level off at a plateau, which indicates long-range pair order (Sec. S4.1).

S3.3 CF states at ν∗=3/2\nu^{*}=3/2: trion Fermi liquid

At α=1/3\alpha=1/3 the CFs couple to u=a+γu=a+\gamma (Sec. S3.1) and see b¯=4​π3​n\bar{b}=\frac{4\pi}{3}n. The lowest level is filled (density 2​n/32n/3) and the second holds n/3n/3, half filling. Integrating out the filled level gives 14​π​u​d​u\frac{1}{4\pi}u\,du. The second-level CFs are in the situation of electrons at ν=1/2\nu=1/2 [70]: attaching two more flux quanta through a field a~\tilde{a}, in the integer form 12​π​a~​d​g−24​π​g​d​g\frac{1}{2\pi}\tilde{a}\,dg-\frac{2}{4\pi}g\,dg (which gives 18​π​a~​d​a~\frac{1}{8\pi}\tilde{a}\,d\tilde{a} when gg is integrated out), makes the final fermions ff see zero average field,

ℒ=ℒf​[u+a~]+14​π​u​d​u+34​π​a​d​a−14​π​γ​d​γ+12​π​Ac​d​a+12​π​a~​d​g−24​π​g​d​g.\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{f}[u+\tilde{a}]+\frac{1}{4\pi}u\,du+\frac{3}{4\pi}a\,da-\frac{1}{4\pi}\gamma\,d\gamma+\frac{1}{2\pi}A_{c}\,da+\frac{1}{2\pi}\tilde{a}\,dg-\frac{2}{4\pi}g\,dg. (S46)

The gauge fields x=(a,γ,a~,g)x=(a,\gamma,\tilde{a},g) enter as 14​π​xT​K​d​x\frac{1}{4\pi}x^{T}K\,dx with the integer matrix K=(4110)⊕(011−2)K=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}4&1\\ 1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\oplus\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\ 1&-2\end{smallmatrix}\bigr), detK=1\det K=1, so all of them are gapped. ff couples to l=(1,1,1,0)l=(1,1,1,0), and lT​K−1​l=0l^{T}K^{-1}l=0: it keeps no statistical interaction. The probe enters through tc=(1,0,0,0)t_{c}=(1,0,0,0), so the charge of ff is −tcT​K−1​l=−1-t_{c}^{T}K^{-1}l=-1, and since tcT​K−1​tc=0t_{c}^{T}K^{-1}t_{c}=0 integrating out xx leaves no Hall response,

ℒ=ℒf​[−Ac],\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{f}[-A_{c}], (S47)

so the trion Fermi liquid has no Hall conductance: the Hall response of the parent FCI is cancelled, as for the Hall crystal (Sec. S3.5). ff carries the physical charge −1-1 of three anyons and couples to no dynamical gauge field: it is a trion of anyons, which has a finite overlap with the physical electron.

S3.4 Color states

Partons.

In the CB gauge we write the boson of flavor bb as ϕb=∑a=1Ncχa​ψa​b\phi_{b}=\sum_{a=1}^{N_{c}}\chi_{a}\psi_{ab}. The decomposition is invariant under χ→U​χ\chi\to U\chi, ψ→U∗​ψ\psi\to U^{*}\psi with U∈U\in U(NcN_{c}), so color is a gauge label and the parton gauge field β\beta is a U(NcN_{c}) field: χ\chi couples to a+βa+\beta and ψ\psi to −βT-\beta^{T}. Since U(NcN_{c})=[SU⁡(Nc)×U⁡(1)]/ℤNc=[\mathrm{SU}(N_{c})\times\mathrm{U}(1)]/\mathbb{Z}_{N_{c}}, β\beta cannot be split into independent SU(NcN_{c}) and U(1) fields with integer fluxes; its trace Tr​β\mathrm{Tr}\,\beta is an ordinary U(1) field, and we write its U(1) part as βc=1Nc​Tr​β\beta_{c}=\frac{1}{N_{c}}\mathrm{Tr}\,\beta. Each color of χ\chi fills the lowest LL of b¯=−2​π​α​n\bar{b}=-2\pi\alpha n at density α​n\alpha n, i.e. at filling 1 with Chern number −1-1, and integrating them out gives the U(NcN_{c})-1 term

−14​π​Tr​[(a+β)​d​(a+β)−2​i3​(a+β)3]=−Nc4​π​a​d​a−Nc2​π​a​d​βc−14​π​Tr​[β​d​β−2​i3​β3].-\frac{1}{4\pi}\mathrm{Tr}\Big[(a+\beta)d(a+\beta)-\tfrac{2\mathrm{i}}{3}(a+\beta)^{3}\Big]=-\frac{N_{c}}{4\pi}a\,da-\frac{N_{c}}{2\pi}a\,d\beta_{c}-\frac{1}{4\pi}\mathrm{Tr}\Big[\beta\,d\beta-\tfrac{2\mathrm{i}}{3}\beta^{3}\Big]. (S48)

With the flux attachment of Eq. (S41), m=1/α=Ncm=1/\alpha=N_{c}, the a​d​aa\,da terms cancel exactly, and aa appears only in 12​π​a​d​(Ac−Nc​βc)\frac{1}{2\pi}a\,d(A_{c}-N_{c}\beta_{c}): it is a Lagrange multiplier that sets βc=Ac/Nc\beta_{c}=A_{c}/N_{c}. This gives Eq. (4). Locally β=β^+βc​𝟙=β^+𝟙ℕ𝕔​𝔸𝕔​𝟙\beta=\hat{\beta}+\beta_{c}\openone=\hat{\beta}+\frac{1}{N_{c}}A_{c}\openone with β^\hat{\beta} traceless: the holons are fermions of charge −1/Nc-1/N_{c} in zero net field, and the U(NcN_{c}) term splits into the FCI response −14​π​Nc​Ac​d​Ac-\frac{1}{4\pi N_{c}}A_{c}\,dA_{c} and SU(NcN_{c})-1 for β^\hat{\beta}. Globally a flux quantum of AcA_{c} comes with a ℤNc\mathbb{Z}_{N_{c}} flux of β^\hat{\beta}, which makes the fractional charge of the holons consistent. The χa\chi_{a} are auxiliary fermions that write the U(NcN_{c})-1 term into a first-quantized anyon wavefunction; for Nc=3N_{c}=3 Eq. (4) is the mirror-orientation form of the parton theory of the doped FCI in Ref. [39].

Projection.

The physical state is the boson amplitude in the parton state, ΦB=⟨0|∏iϕbi​(𝐫i)​|Φχ⟩|Φψ⟩\Phi_{B}=\langle 0|\prod_{i}\phi_{b_{i}}(\mathbf{r}_{i})|\Phi_{\chi}\rangle|\Phi_{\psi}\rangle. Expanding every ϕb\phi_{b} gives one term per coloring a=(a1,…,aN)a=(a_{1},\dots,a_{N}). Each color level holds exactly k=N/Nck=N/N_{c} fermions, so only colorings with |Sc​(a)|=k|S_{c}(a)|=k survive, and the χ\chi factor is sgn⁡(a)​∏cV¯Sc​(a)\mathrm{sgn}(a)\prod_{c}\bar{V}_{S_{c}(a)}, with sgn⁡(a)\mathrm{sgn}(a) the sign of the permutation that sorts the particles by color. This gives Eq. (2); without the sign, Bose symmetry is lost. Each anyon sees α⁡(N−1)\alpha(N-1) statistical flux quanta and has k−1k-1 antivortices in ∏cV¯Sc\prod_{c}\bar{V}_{S_{c}}, one on every other anyon of its color, so the holons see no field in the thermodynamic limit. Every antivortex sits on an anyon: these states have no free vortices and are liquids.

Products and hyperdeterminants.

If color is locked to flavor, ai=bia_{i}=b_{i}, only one coloring survives, and by Eq. (S22) the state is in the CF gauge with one extra winding between flavors, the flux attachment K=(2−1−12)K=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}2&-1\\ -1&2\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) of a U(1)2 theory: a product of parton determinants. A color-symmetric holon state keeps all colorings, and the color sum is a hyperdeterminant [71, 72, 73], #P-hard to evaluate in general [74]. We evaluate it exactly in a polarization form: a polarization identity [75] and the Cauchy–Binet formula and its Pfaffian version [76] turn it into a signed sum of 2N−32^{N-3} determinants (metals) or Pfaffians (pairing states) for SU(3), instead of ∼3N\sim 3^{N} colorings.

Descendants of the holon metal.

The phases of Eq. (4) are derived in Ref. [39]; Table S1 lists those we study. In the parent SU(3) holon metal each of the nine species ψa​b\psi_{ab} fills a Fermi sea of density n/9n/9. Color-flavor-locked pairing gives the color superconductor, Φψ=Pf⁡[σi​j​g​(ξi,ξj)]\Phi_{\psi}=\mathrm{Pf}[\sigma_{ij}g(\xi_{i},\xi_{j})] with σi​j=∑AϵA​ai​aj​ϵA​bi​bj\sigma_{ij}=\sum_{A}\epsilon_{Aa_{i}a_{j}}\epsilon_{Ab_{i}b_{j}}, which locks color rotations to flavor rotations, SU(3)c×{}_{c}\timesSU(3)f→{}_{f}\toSU(3)diag [91, 92], and Higgses the gauge field completely; its gauge-invariant order parameter, a color singlet of three pairs, binds six anyons with charge 6​q=−26q=-2. Adjoint Higgs fields that lock the color index to the flavor index reduce SU(3) to U(1)2, which gives the U(1)2 metal and, with inter-flavor pairing, the U(1)2 superconductor, or to Z3, which gives the Type I triplet and the singlet Z3 metals.

Chirality and chiral central charge.

Our calculations have the orientation of tMoTe2 (Sec. S3.5): the parent FCI of Eq. (S41) has σx​y=−13e2/h\sigma_{xy}=-\frac{1}{3}\,e^{2}/h, as the doped FCI of the ν=2/3\nu=2/3 state, and Eq. (4) is the mirror image of the theory of Ref. [39], whose FCI has σx​y=+13e2/h\sigma_{xy}=+\frac{1}{3}\,e^{2}/h.

We label a paired state by the winding ℓ\ell of ⟨ψ𝐤​ψ−𝐤⟩∝ei​ℓ​ϑ𝐤\langle\psi_{\mathbf{k}}\psi_{-\mathbf{k}}\rangle\propto\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\ell\vartheta_{\mathbf{k}}}, the eigenvalue of Lz=−i∂ϑL_{z}=-\mathrm{i}\partial_{\vartheta}. A weakly paired pocket has BdG Chern number −ℓ-\ell and contributes c−=−ℓ/2c_{-}=-\ell/2 [39], in the orientation in which a filled LL in a positive field contributes +1+1. A J=0J=0 pair in holon flux 2​Qψ2Q_{\psi} has ℓ=2​Qψ\ell=2Q_{\psi}, so the color superconductor is p−i​pp-ip (ℓ=−1\ell=-1) at qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 and p+i​pp+ip at qb​g=5/3q_{bg}=5/3. The Chern–Simons term selects ℓ=−1\ell=-1 in our orientation [39], the sector in which the color superconductor lies furthest below the crystal (Sec. S4.3). With SU(3) Higgsed completely, the three χ\chi levels contribute 3×(−1)3\times(-1) and the nine holon pockets 9×129\times\frac{1}{2}: the doped FCI contributes c−=32c_{-}=\frac{3}{2}, and with the filled C=1C=1 band of the ν=2/3\nu=2/3 state c−=52c_{-}=\frac{5}{2}. Three anyons make one carrier of the parent FCI, c∼ψ†​ψ†​ψ†c\sim\psi^{\dagger}\psi^{\dagger}\psi^{\dagger} up to the filled χ\chi levels, so the charge-2​e2e pairs have angular momentum L=−3​ℓ=3L=-3\ell=3: they are f+i​ff+if [39]. A BCS superconductor of the same carriers with the same L=3L=3 has one pocket with c−=−32c_{-}=-\frac{3}{2}, and with the ν=1\nu=1 integer quantum Hall background of the filled C=1C=1 band (the block K=1K=1 of the ν=2/3\nu=2/3 state) c−=1−32=−12c_{-}=1-\frac{3}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}. The two superconductors have the same pairing symmetry, but their c−c_{-} differ by 3.

Semions: the two-color superconductor.

For Nc=2N_{c}=2 the same construction, with βc=Ac/2\beta_{c}=A_{c}/2, leaves color doublets of charge −1/2-1/2 coupled to SU(2)-1, at holon flux 2​Qψ=qb​g−122Q_{\psi}=q_{bg}-\frac{1}{2}. A J=0J=0 pair in flux 2​Qψ2Q_{\psi} has relative angular momentum 2​Qψ2Q_{\psi} in the planar coordinate zz (holomorphic for 2​Qψ>02Q_{\psi}>0), so the closed-shell sectors qb​g=−3/2q_{bg}=-3/2 (spinless) and −1/2-1/2 [SU(2)] give d−i​dd-id and p−i​pp-ip pairs (ℓ=−2\ell=-2 and −1-1 in the notation above). Color-singlet pairing, Φψ=Pf⁡[ϵai​aj​gi​j]\Phi_{\psi}=\mathrm{Pf}[\epsilon_{a_{i}a_{j}}g_{ij}] (spinless, d−i​dd-id) or Pf⁡[ϵai​aj​ϵfi​fj​gi​j]\mathrm{Pf}[\epsilon_{a_{i}a_{j}}\epsilon_{f_{i}f_{j}}g_{ij}] [SU(2), spin-singlet p−i​pp-ip], gives a condensate of charge −1-1, a pair of semions, which leads to the same paired superfluid phase as in the CF ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 description. The final phase has chiral central charge c−=0c_{-}=0: the two χ\chi levels contribute 2×(−1)2\times(-1), the paired holon pockets 2×12\times 1 (spinless, ℓ=−2\ell=-2) or 4×124\times\frac{1}{2} [SU(2), ℓ=−1\ell=-1], and the color SU(2), whose level −1-1 the chiral holons cancel, confines and adds nothing. A pair of semions is one boson of the parent, so the phase is an ordinary superfluid of these bosons, without topological order: the chiral edge mode of the parent Laughlin state is gone. For SU(2) semions the spin sector stays chiral, with the spin Hall response of Sec. S3.2, and the charge sector compensates it in c−c_{-}.

S3.5 CB crystals: Hall crystals and skyrmions

Hall response.

Let the parent FCI have K-matrix KK, charge vector tt, and anyons of gauge charge ll,

ℒ=−14​π​KI​J​aI​d​aJ+12​π​tI​Ac​d​aI+ℒϕ​[l⋅a],\mathcal{L}=-\frac{1}{4\pi}K_{IJ}a_{I}da_{J}+\frac{1}{2\pi}t_{I}A_{c}\,da_{I}+\mathcal{L}_{\phi}[l\cdot a], (S49)

so that σFCI=tT​K−1​t\sigma_{\rm FCI}=t^{T}K^{-1}t in units of e2/he^{2}/h, the anyon charge is q=tT​K−1​lq=t^{T}K^{-1}l and its statistics θ/π=lT​K−1​l\theta/\pi=l^{T}K^{-1}l. Represent the anyons by bosons ϕ\phi, as in the CB gauge; all flavors carry the same ll. A pinned vortex lattice of the ϕ\phi condensate freezes the flux of l⋅al\cdot a. Imposing this with a multiplier Λ\Lambda and a term 12​π​Λ​d​(l⋅a)\frac{1}{2\pi}\Lambda\,d(l\cdot a) enlarges K→K′=(K−l−lT0)K\to K^{\prime}=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}K&-l\\ -l^{T}&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) with t′=(t,0)t^{\prime}=(t,0), and block inversion gives

σx​y=t′T​K′−1​t′=σFCI−q2θ/π\sigma_{xy}=t^{\prime T}K^{\prime-1}t^{\prime}=\sigma_{\rm FCI}-\frac{q^{2}}{\theta/\pi} (S50)

For the Laughlin parent of Eq. (S41) the same steps, with 12​π​Λ​d​a\frac{1}{2\pi}\Lambda\,da, give Λ=−Ac\Lambda=-A_{c} and leave no Ac​d​AcA_{c}\,dA_{c} term. The crystal adds σa=−q2/α\sigma_{a}=-q^{2}/\alpha. If the parent state is a Laughlin FCI (K=mK=m, q=1/mq=1/m, θ=π/m\theta=\pi/m), this gives σx​y=0\sigma_{xy}=0. For the ν=2/3\nu=2/3 parent FCI, with K=diag⁡(1,−3)K=\mathrm{diag}(1,-3) and t=(1,1)t=(1,1), whose charge-e/3e/3 anyons l=(0,1)l=(0,1) have θ=−π/3\theta=-\pi/3, we get σx​y=(23+13)​e2/h=e2/h\sigma_{xy}=(\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3})\,e^{2}/h=e^{2}/h.

Skyrmions.

With flavor vortices each flavor has its own antivortices. Moving one anyon to 𝐫\mathbf{r} with the others fixed, its amplitudes za​(𝐫)z_{a}(\mathbf{r}) to carry flavor aa (labels taken from a reference anyon at fixed positions) define a point [z1:z2:z3]∈CP2[z_{1}\!:\!z_{2}\!:\!z_{3}]\in\mathrm{CP}^{2} in which every flavor-blind factor cancels. Where zaz_{a} has a vortex the other flavors fill the core, so the vortices are coreless and the map has a skyrmion density. Its total, the skyrmion number, equals NvN_{v} when the three vortex sublattices interleave, and one skyrmion then binds one vortex of each flavor, 1/α=31/\alpha=3 anyons. The Hall response is that of Eq. (S50): the state is a skyrmion Hall crystal, with σx​y=e2/h\sigma_{xy}=e^{2}/h for the ν=2/3\nu=2/3 parent of tMoTe2.

S4 Numerical results

S4.1 Semions

Energies.

Table S2 lists E/NE/N of every ansatz in the closed-shell CF sectors of Fig. 1. The CF ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 state, the CF networks started from random orbitals and the two-color superconductor agree to within about 0.0050.005 per particle at every size. The two-color superconductor lies within 0.0020.002 of the best liquid at N=8N=8–12, and the attention networks give the lowest liquid energies at several sizes, e.g. 0.51790.5179 against 0.52070.5207 for the CF state for SU(2) at N=24N=24. The random starts stay rotation invariant up to N=24N=24. At N=32N=32 (spinless) the message-passing network ends in a non-uniform state (⟨L2⟩=17\langle L^{2}\rangle=17) slightly above the CF state, while the attention network is nearly uniform (⟨L2⟩=3.4\langle L^{2}\rangle=3.4) and degenerate with it; at N=40N=40 both random starts are strongly non-uniform (⟨L2⟩≈100\langle L^{2}\rangle\approx 100–140) and lie 0.060.06 higher: the random start enters the crystal phase. The CB network lies 0.120.12 (spinless) and 0.220.22 [SU(2)] above the liquids at N=24N=24, and the CB vortex lattice higher still.

Overlaps.

To test whether these liquids are one phase we compute the fidelity F=|⟨A|B⟩|2/(⟨A|A⟩​⟨B|B⟩)F=|\langle A|B\rangle|^{2}/(\langle A|A\rangle\langle B|B\rangle) of pairs of trained states with their full anyonic amplitudes (Table S3), estimated as F=|⟨B/A⟩|A|2|2/⟨|B/A|2⟩|A|2F=|\langle B/A\rangle_{|A|^{2}}|^{2}/\langle|B/A|^{2}\rangle_{|A|^{2}} on samples of AA and checked with the two-sided estimator ⟨B/A⟩|A|2​⟨A/B⟩|B|2\langle B/A\rangle_{|A|^{2}}\langle A/B\rangle_{|B|^{2}}. The CF ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 state, the random-start networks and the two-color superconductor have mutual fidelities 0.950.95–0.9970.997 at N=8N=8 and 12, although they are built in different ways: CF Landau levels, a color sum of partons in the CB gauge, and networks without either structure. Their fidelity with the CB crystal is 0.020.02–0.50.5 and falls quickly with NN. The independent liquid ansatzes therefore describe one state.

Disk.

As a check of the sphere results we use planar versions of the same ansatzes on a disk with a hard wall (Fig. S4). The CF liquid lies far below the CB vortex state at every NN, by 0.180.18 (spinless) and 0.420.42 [SU(2)] at N=30N=30. The edge contributes at order N−1/2N^{-1/2}, and the fit E/N=e∞+a/N+b/NE/N=e_{\infty}+a/\sqrt{N}+b/N of the CF liquid over N=6N=6–56 gives e∞=0.809​(17)e_{\infty}=0.809(17) (spinless) and 0.557​(10)0.557(10) [SU(2)], within two standard errors of the sphere values 0.7837​(4)0.7837(4) and 0.5407​(7)0.5407(7).

Pair correlator.

The pair density matrix ρ2​(R,R′)=⟨Δ†​(R′)​Δ​(R)⟩\rho_{2}(R,R^{\prime})=\langle\Delta^{\dagger}(R^{\prime})\Delta(R)\rangle, with Δ⁡(R)\Delta(R) removing two anyons near RR, is estimated in the trained state by moving a pair rigidly. For a configuration ZZ sampled from |Ψ|2|\Psi|^{2} we pick an anyon at random and its nearest partner within c2=0.6n−1/2c_{2}=0.6\,n^{-1/2} (for SU(2), of the opposite or of the same spin), and rotate both by an angle γ\gamma about the axis through the center of the sphere perpendicular to the pair’s center, so that the pair moves along a great circle by the arc length R​γR\gamma with its internal configuration unchanged. With ZγZ_{\gamma} the moved configuration,

C2​(γ)=⟨Φ⁡(Zγ)Φ⁡(Z)​ei⁡[S⁡(Zγ)−S⁡(Z)]⟩|Ψ|2,S=∑j∉pair[2​αs​arg⁡wc​j+αs​∑a∈pairarg⁡wa​jwc​j],C_{2}(\gamma)=\Big\langle\frac{\Phi(Z_{\gamma})}{\Phi(Z)}\,\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}[S(Z_{\gamma})-S(Z)]}\Big\rangle_{|\Psi|^{2}},\qquad S=\sum_{j\notin{\rm pair}}\Big[2\alpha_{s}\arg w_{cj}+\alpha_{s}\sum_{a\in{\rm pair}}\arg\frac{w_{aj}}{w_{cj}}\Big], (S51)

where Φ\Phi is the wavefunction without the statistical factor and SS the phase of the statistical factor between the pair and the other anyons jj, written with the spinor ξc\xi_{c} of the pair’s center, wc​j=uc​vj−vc​ujw_{cj}=u_{c}v_{j}-v_{c}u_{j}. Factors between unmoved anyons and the internal factor of the pair are unchanged by the move. Since 2​αs2\alpha_{s} is an integer for semions, the first term of SS is single valued, and the second, with ratios close to 1 for a compact pair, is evaluated on the principal branch: SS is the string of the local pair operator ψ⁡(z1)​ψ​(z2)\psi(z_{1})\psi(z_{2}), with its branch cut inside the pair, and C2C_{2} is the normalized pair density matrix, C2​(0)=1C_{2}(0)=1. A string accumulated member by member along the path differs from it by −1-1 for every anyon that passes between the two members and suppresses a genuine condensate. We average over 3×1033\times 10^{3}–2.5×1042.5\times 10^{4} pairs per size and define the plateau as the mean of |C2||C_{2}| over the outer half of the move, γ≥π/2\gamma\geq\pi/2.

Figure S5 shows |C2||C_{2}| of the CF ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 state at all sizes. After a drop over one to two interparticle spacings it levels off. The plateau is 0.0780.078, 0.0750.075, 0.0630.063, 0.0660.066, 0.0590.059 and 0.0690.069 at N=12N=12, 16, 20, 24, 32 and 40 for spinless semions, and 0.370.37, 0.360.36, 0.320.32 and 0.340.34 at N=12N=12–24 for opposite-spin pairs of SU(2) semions; both fall only as about N−0.16N^{-0.16}, against N−1/2N^{-1/2} for the bare state (Sec. S3.2). Same-spin pairs of SU(2) semions decay to zero. These sizes cannot separate a plateau from a slow power law; the evidence for a superfluid is the structure of the state, the cancellation of the Chern–Simons term and the energetics.

Structure factor.

The density structure factor S⁡(l)=1N​∑i​jPl​(cos⁡θi​j)S(l)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{ij}P_{l}(\cos\theta_{ij}) at q=l/Rq=l/R is shown in Fig. S6. At N=12N=12 the CF ν∗=2\nu^{*}=2 state, the random-start networks and the two-color superconductor have the same S⁡(q)S(q), to within 0.010.01 (spinless) and 0.020.02 [SU(2)], as their overlaps (Table S3) require; at this size the crystal’s S⁡(q)S(q) is still close to theirs. At the smallest wave vector q1=1/Rq_{1}=1/R the CF state has S⁡(q1)/q1​ℓ∗=0.51S(q_{1})/q_{1}\ell^{*}=0.51–0.570.57 (spinless, N=8N=8–40) and 0.600.60–0.650.65 [SU(2), N=8N=8–24], nearly independent of NN, while S⁡(q1)/(q1​ℓ∗)2S(q_{1})/(q_{1}\ell^{*})^{2} grows with NN: S⁡(q)S(q) is linear in qq, as for a superfluid with a sound mode, rather than quadratic, as for an incompressible quantum Hall state such as the bare CF state.

S4.2 Spinless anyons at θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3

The shift sectors qb​g=−5/3q_{bg}=-5/3, −4/3-4/3, −1-1 and −1/3-1/3 select the Moore–Read state, the CFL, the PH-Pfaffian and the anti-Pfaffian in the second CF level, and the CF liquid of each sector is started from that exact wavefunction. Table S4 compares every ansatz with the CB crystal of the same sector and size. At N≥12N\geq 12 the best liquid and the crystal lie within 0.0150.015 per particle, from −0.013-0.013 (Moore–Read sector, N=14N=14) to +0.008+0.008 (PH-Pfaffian sector, N=16N=16), with signs that change with the sector and with NN; in the CFL sector the trion Fermi liquid is lower by 0.0100.010 at N=24N=24. The CF networks from random orbitals end in non-uniform states above both. The color states with three colors, the three-color metal and its 2SC descendants (colors 1 and 2 paired, color 3 a closed-shell pocket or paired with itself), are the lowest states at N≤9N\leq 9. At N=12N=12 they lie slightly below the crystal in the sectors qb​g=2/3q_{bg}=2/3 and 5/35/3, where no CF liquid exists, while in the anti-Pfaffian sector the CF liquid is lower.

S4.3 SU(3) anyons at θ=π/3\theta=\pi/3

Result.

Starting from the SU(3) holon metal, we consider its descendants (Table S1) in several shift sectors qb​gq_{bg}, together with the skyrmion Hall crystal and general CF networks. The color superconductor has the lowest energy. In the sector qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 it lies 0.0220.022, 0.0410.041 and 0.0540.054 below the skyrmion Hall crystal at N=6N=6, 12 and 18, and it extrapolates to e∞=0.498​(1)e_{\infty}=0.498(1), against 0.572​(2)0.572(2) for the crystal (Table 1); in the opposite chirality, qb​g=5/3q_{bg}=5/3, it lies 0.0040.004 and 0.0210.021 below the crystal at N=12N=12 and 18. Different sectors differ only at order 1/N1/N, as the crystal shows: it extrapolates to 0.572​(2)0.572(2), 0.560​(5)0.560(5), 0.562​(4)0.562(4) and 0.542​(5)0.542(5) at qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3, 2/32/3, 5/35/3 and 8/38/3 [Fig. S7(a)]. We therefore compare the energy of each phase with that of the crystal at the same qb​gq_{bg} and NN, to remove this 1/N1/N finite-size effect (Table S5). The advantage of the color superconductor does not come from the size of its network. The projected state without variational freedom has E/N=2.12E/N=2.12, 1.83 and 1.43 at N=6N=6, 12 and 18, poor at short distances, but with only a two-body Jastrow factor, the pair matrix and the holon orbitals (616 parameters at N=6N=6, 1 640 at N=12N=12) it already reaches 0.4200.420 and 0.4840.484, below the crystal networks (0.4260.426 and 0.4920.492 with 15 182 and 16 910 parameters).

Other phases.

All other states we tried lie higher in energy, and those we compared at N≥12N\geq 12, except the parent holon metal, have almost zero overlap with the color superconductor. As for semions, the overlap is the fidelity FF with the color superconductor of the same size at qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 (Table S6); the same state with only a two-body Jastrow factor, the same-phase reference, keeps F=0.96F=0.96 at N=6N=6 and 0.920.92 at N=12N=12. The bare projection, without any Jastrow factor or backflow, has F=0.011F=0.011 at N=6N=6 and 0.00010.0001 at N=12N=12: the fidelity vanishes as well between two states of the same phase that differ strongly at short distances, as the bare state does from the trained one (E/N=2.12E/N=2.12 and 1.83 against 0.40 and 0.45).

Its fidelity with the color superconductor is F=0.69F=0.69, as expected for a weakly paired state and its parent Fermi sea in a small system.

Their fidelity with the color superconductor is F≈0.2F\approx 0.2 at N=6N=6, where the space of states is small, and F≲10−4F\lesssim 10^{-4} at N=12N=12 and 18.

The Type II triplet Z3 metal fits only the sector qb​g=8/3q_{bg}=8/3, which has no color superconductor, and lies far above the crystal there: E/N=1.05E/N=1.05 (N=12N=12) and 1.121.12 (N=27N=27) when rotation invariant, against 0.3490.349 and 0.4540.454, and 0.5870.587 and 0.6570.657 with feature-dependent orbitals, which break rotation invariance; on the disk it lies 0.160.16–0.180.18 above the crystal at N=24N=24–30.

At N≥12N\geq 12 they lose rotation invariance, lie above the crystal and have F≲0.002F\lesssim 0.002.

Z3 metals.

We study one SU(3)-singlet Z3 metal and two different triplet Z3 metals. In the singlet Z3 metal the holons, with color locked to flavor, form one pocket, the flavor singlet tr​ψ\mathrm{tr}\,\psi (Sec. S1.3). The Type I triplet Z3 metal is the color construction with three pockets ηA=ϵA​a​b​ψa​b/2\eta_{A}=\epsilon_{Aab}\psi_{ab}/\sqrt{2}, which lock color to flavor only partially: since ϵA​a​b\epsilon_{Aab} needs AA, aa and bb all different, an anyon of flavor bb can carry either of the two other colors, each in a different pocket, so Eq. (2) keeps two colorings per anyon and remains a color sum, of ∑x(kx)3\sum_{x}\binom{k}{x}^{3} balanced colorings (346 at N=12N=12, 15 184 at N=18N=18). A single coloring survives only when color equals flavor, as in the U(1)2 states and the singlet Z3 metal; locking color to flavor through a fixed permutation is a relabeling of the colors, a gauge transformation, and gives those states again. The Type II triplet Z3 metal is the construction of Ref. [37]: the anyon is ΦI=ΨI​d\Phi_{I}=\Psi_{I}d, with an SU(3)-singlet fermion dd that fills three Landau levels of the CB field and the triplet ΨI\Psi_{I} in three Fermi seas, so that ΦB=χ¯3∏IdetI\Phi_{B}=\bar{\chi}_{3}\prod_{I}\det_{I} is a single product with no color sum. Its flux counting puts it in a different sector from Type I: dd fills exactly three levels, and the Fermi seas see zero flux, only at qb​g=8/3q_{bg}=8/3, where they close at N=12N=12 and 27, whereas Type I lives at qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 and 2/32/3.

Closed shells.

The states with Fermi pockets are evaluated where every pocket is a closed shell, so that they are rotation invariant. The shells of a pocket are set by the holon flux 2​Qψ=qb​g−2/32Q_{\psi}=q_{bg}-2/3: at qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 (2​Qψ=−12Q_{\psi}=-1) they hold 2,4,6,…2,4,6,\dots holons, so a pocket is closed when it holds 2,6,12,…2,6,12,\dots holons; at qb​g=2/3q_{bg}=2/3 (2​Qψ=02Q_{\psi}=0) they hold 1,3,5,…1,3,5,\dots, and a pocket is closed with 1,4,9,…1,4,9,\dots holons. The allowed NN follow from the number of pockets: nine pockets of N/9N/9 holons for the SU(3) holon metal, closed at N=18N=18 (qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3) and N=9N=9 (qb​g=2/3q_{bg}=2/3); three pockets of N/3N/3 for the Type I triplet Z3 metal and the U(1)2 metal, closed at N=6N=6, 18, 36 (qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3) and N=3N=3, 12, 27 (qb​g=2/3q_{bg}=2/3); one pocket of all NN holons for the singlet Z3 metal, closed at N=6N=6, 12, 30, 42 (qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3). The pairing states need no closed shell, but they need the holon flux ∓1\mp 1 of the two chiralities p−i​pp-ip and p+i​pp+ip, i.e. qb​g=−1/3q_{bg}=-1/3 or 5/35/3.

S4.4 Skyrmion Hall crystal

Figure S8 shows the crystal at N=36N=36. The vortices are found by moving one particle of a flavor over a grid while the other particles stay at a configuration sampled from |Ψ|2|\Psi|^{2}. They are not fixed parameters of the network: the backflow and the environment-dependent coefficients of Eq. (S20) move them with the other particles, so they shift from one sampled configuration to the next. Over 48 configurations the vortices of each flavor cluster around NvN_{v} fixed lattice sites: their rms distance from the site is 0.2–0.4a0a_{0}, against site spacings of 1.2–1.5a0a_{0} (N=12N=12–36). The vortex lattice is thus well defined, and the vortices fluctuate about their sites, as the particles of a quantum crystal do about theirs. The three sublattices interleave, so every vortex core is filled by the other two flavors, as in the interlaced vortex lattices of two-component condensates [93]. Each flavor’s density vanishes at its sites and rises to about twice its mean in between, while the total density varies by only about ±10%\pm 10\%: the crystal is a texture of the flavors, not of the charge. The CP2 map has |Qsk|=Nv|Q_{\rm sk}|=N_{v} in 46 of 48 configurations (Nv−1N_{v}-1 in the other two), each vortex cell carries a skyrmion charge 1/31/3 on average, its configuration-averaged composition reproduces the measured flavor densities (correlation 0.99), and its averaged skyrmion density is highest where the total density dips (correlation −0.94-0.94). The same structure appears at N=12N=12–36 and at qb​g=5/3q_{bg}=5/3. Without the texture the crystal is flavor symmetric, with the energy of spinless anyons, 0.11–0.13 higher per particle at N=12N=12–24 [Fig. S8(d)]. The skyrmion crystal is the SU(3) analog of quantum Hall and spinor-condensate skyrmion crystals [94, 95, 96, 93]. In the doped FCI of twisted MoTe2 the SU(3) flavor is a valley index: translations act projectively on the charge-e/3e/3 anyons, which makes the anyon band threefold degenerate, with three valleys [21, 24, 38]. The flavor texture therefore breaks the moiré translation symmetry, and the skyrmion Hall crystal should be visible to local probes as a charge order on the moiré scale.
